Purpose and exclusions

Friends and block lists are durable identity relationships. Presence is an authorized projection, not a durable promise that a particular actor remains loaded. Account recovery belongs to the authentication provider/service, not an NPC or local save edit.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Define account-versus-character relationship semantics in DA_SocialPolicy_Default; do not mix them opportunistically across features.
  2. Create DB_social_edges, DB_social_edges and DB_social_edges with uniqueness constraints and deletion/retention policy.
  3. Build WBP_Social with requests, friends, blocked list, private-message and invite controls; blocked actions are clearly disabled.
  4. Reopen chat/party/trade to consult the same block policy rather than copied lists. Add account recovery link to WBP_Login, not a game-side password reset implementation.
  5. Test cross-zone presence and logout lease expiry with two accounts.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Friends, presence, blocking and account recovery. Rule owner: URPGSocialComponent. This asset’s role is Friends and block lists are durable identity relationships. Presence is an authorized projection, not a durable promise that a particular actor remains loaded. Account recovery belongs to the authentication provider/service, not an NPC or local save edit.

  1. Player finds a character through a bounded name/identity lookup; server applies privacy and rate limits without exposing account secrets.
  2. Friend request records are authenticated and deduplicated; acceptance creates the authorized bilateral relationship.
  3. Block writes take precedence and immediately invalidate delivery/invite/trade eligibility according to policy.
  4. Presence combines active session leases and user privacy settings; it expires when a lease ends rather than persisting a stale Online flag.
  5. WBP_Social updates from service results and local notifications; actor references are resolved only for currently relevant in-zone players.
  6. Recovery opens the configured provider flow; after identity is regained, load the same durable account/characters through normal validation.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: SocialFixture_AB / Character_A / Character_B. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Duplicate request -> one request, no notification spam.
Blocked target gets invite/trade/private message -> denied by common policy.
Presence cache stale after crash -> expires; no secret zone/online disclosure beyond privacy policy.
Recover wrong provider account -> cannot access another AccountId's characters.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
